Section 5 keeps rounding, the useful central-density bound, one-arc repair, and the two-move progress argument. Section 6 explains the finite update and monotone enclosure. Section 7 retains the finite horizon and clocked parameter selection. Geometry, certificate calibration, refinement estimates, consistency details and arithmetic inventories are in appendices. Section 8 states the production and initial-partial-order corollaries and the principal open direction; Appendix G proves the strengthened prefix count and both initializations. implementation_change: The answer-selection loop refines only queried labels after a failed certificate, at most twice, using the middle half directly. After recording the answer, one complete path batch in path order or one degree repair restores the strict bounds. Refine passes its reason to ChooseAnchor, which uses central certification only for structural repairs. Normalize propagates all bounds in two topological passes. RoundUp replaces minimum-depth anchor search. The rarity bound gives P=O(Q(n)/k+n) including an unfinished call; stored precision is O(n log^2 n).

consequences.production: One target-independent adversary forces (1-epsilon_n) I(R) - epsilon_n n comparisons, epsilon_n -> 0, where I(R)=log(n!)-log e(R).
consequences.prefix_count: Auxiliary weights (2/k)w(c) give log N_ord >= log(n!) - n[-log(1-1/k)] - (1+O(log k/k))q after any completed recursive prefix.
consequences.initial_partial_order: Compatible weak-order extension and independent layer adversaries at the common ambient parameter k(n) force (1-o(1))log e(P)-O(n log log(n+2)) comparisons.
consequences.alternative_initialization: A deterministic partial-order producer runs against the ordinary adversary; the saved state, with relabelled queries, forces log e(P)-o(n log n) further comparisons.
